summary:
The Preventing the Financing of Illegal Synthetic Drugs Act, Pub. L. 118-79, establishes a congressional mandate for a Government Accountability Office study and report concerning illicit finance associated with trafficking synthetic drugs into or affecting the United States. The Act does not amend the United States Code, create a programmatic enforcement authority, authorize appropriations, or appropriate funds.

Section 1 designates the short title as the “Preventing the Financing of Illegal Synthetic Drugs Act.” Section 2 sets forth congressional findings regarding overdose deaths involving synthetic opioids; the growth of synthetic drugs or new psychoactive substances; the economics of fentanyl trafficking; and the role of financial flows in sustaining organized criminal activity.

Section 3(a) requires the Comptroller General of the United States to carry out a study on illicit financing in connection with trafficking of specified synthetic drugs and related substances, including fentanyl and methamphetamine, fentanyl- and methamphetamine-related substances, Captagon, and fentanyl and methamphetamine precursors. The required study must include: the business of synthetic-drug trafficking and related illicit finance, including participation by transnational criminal organizations and terror syndicates and notable trafficking corridors, source countries, and transit countries; business models used by such organizations, including domestic and foreign activities relating to precursor purchase or production, supply-chain movement, manufacture, marketing, distribution, sales, and return of proceeds; overlap between human-trafficking business models and synthetic-drug trafficking and related illicit finance; use of online illicit drug markets and social media for marketing, sale, and payment; financial methods used by transnational criminal organizations, including payment, money laundering, and repatriation of proceeds; use of specified social media and payment applications, including Snapchat, Discord, Facebook, and CashApp, to facilitate financial transactions for synthetic-drug trafficking, especially among young people; and U.S. Government activities to combat illicit finance related to synthetic-drug trafficking.

With respect to U.S. Government activities, section 3(a)(7) specifically requires review of interagency collaboration, including personnel detailed to other agencies; intergovernmental collaboration; intersectoral collaboration with the private sector, including business and nongovernmental communities; and identified gaps or resource deficiencies in the coordination and collaboration activities described.

Section 3(b) requires the Comptroller General, not later than one year after enactment—i.e., by September 13, 2025—to issue to Congress a report containing all findings and determinations made in carrying out the study.
